easy.explanation: Proverbs 16:1 says, “the answer of the tongue, is from the LORD.”
easy.q: From whom does the answer of the tongue come?

easy.explanation: The verse says, “the LORD weigheth the spirits.”
Proverbs 16:3 says, “Commit thy works unto the LORD.”
easy.q: What should a person commit unto the LORD?

medium.explanation: Although a man’s ways may seem clean in his own eyes, “the LORD weigheth the spirits.”
medium.q: What happens even though a man may think all his ways are clean?

medium.explanation: In this context, “weigheth” means that the LORD examines and evaluates the inner spirit.
medium.q: What does “weigheth” mean in “the LORD weigheth the spirits”?

medium.explanation: Proverbs 16:3 says, “and thy thoughts shall be established.”
medium.q: What is promised after a person commits his works unto the LORD?

answers: People plan and act, but the LORD directs and establishes
challenge.explanation: These verses show human planning and action while attributing direction and establishment to the LORD.
challenge.q: What common idea appears in verses 1, 3, and 9?

answers: A little with righteousness is better than great revenues without right
challenge.explanation: Proverbs 16:8 says, “Better is a little with righteousness than great revenues without right.”
challenge.q: What does the proverb teach about wealth acquired with righteousness?

answers: Mercy, truth, and the fear of the LORD
challenge.explanation: The passage emphasizes mercy and truth, the fear of the LORD, turning from evil, and pleasing the LORD.
challenge.q: Which combination describes the desired way of life in verses 5–7?

easy.explanation: Proverbs 16:10 says, “his mouth transgresseth not in judgment.”
easy.q: What does the king’s mouth not transgress in?

easy.explanation: The verse presents a just weight and balance as belonging to the LORD and representing righteous judgment.
easy.q: What do a just weight and balance represent?

easy.explanation: Proverbs 16:16 says, “How much better is it to get wisdom than gold!” and to choose understanding rather than silver.
easy.q: What is better to get than gold?

medium.explanation: Proverbs 16:12 says, “the throne is established by righteousness.”
A just weight and balance are fair instruments used for honest measurement.
medium.q: What is a “just weight and balance”?

medium.explanation: Proverbs 16:12 says that it is an abomination to kings to commit wickedness, and the surrounding verses warn of royal wrath.
medium.q: What may bring the wrath of a king?

answers: Righteousness and favor versus wickedness and wrath
challenge.explanation: The passage praises righteous kingship while warning about wickedness and the danger of a king’s wrath.
challenge.q: What central contrast appears concerning the king?

answers: The king’s speech carries moral responsibility
The king’s words have no effect
challenge.explanation: The king’s mouth and lips are associated with judgment, righteousness, and speaking what is right.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from the connection between the king’s lips, judgment, and righteousness?

challenge.explanation: Proverbs 16:14 says, “a wise man will pacify it.”
challenge.q: What can a wise man do concerning the wrath of a king?

paragraphs.title: Turning from Evil, Humility, and Trust

easy.explanation: Proverbs 16:17 says, “The highway of the upright is to depart from evil.”
easy.q: What does the highway of the upright depart from?

easy.explanation: The verse says, “Pride goeth before destruction.”

answers: The person who trusteth in the LORD
The person who takes a city
easy.explanation: Proverbs 16:20 says, “whoso trusteth in the LORD, happy is he.”
easy.q: Who is happy according to the passage?

answers: The person who keeps his way preserves his soul
The soul has no connection with conduct
medium.explanation: The verse says, “he that keepeth his way preserveth his soul.”
medium.q: How are keeping one’s way and preserving one’s soul connected?

medium.explanation: A haughty spirit is a proud or self-exalting attitude.

answers: Being of an humble spirit with the lowly
medium.explanation: Proverbs 16:19 says it is better “to be of an humble spirit with the lowly” than to divide spoil with the proud.
medium.q: What is better than dividing the spoil with the proud?

answers: Depart from evil, avoid pride, and choose humility
challenge.explanation: The passage moves from departing from evil to warnings about pride and the preference for humility.
challenge.q: What sequence of ideas appears in verses 17–19?

answers: Pride is presented as coming before destruction and a fall
challenge.explanation: The passage says, “Pride goeth before destruction,” and “an haughty spirit before a fall.”
challenge.q: What is the relationship between pride and failure?

answers: Wise conduct, understanding, and trust in the LORD
challenge.explanation: The passage commends handling a matter wisely and trusting in the LORD.
challenge.q: What combination brings good and happiness in the passage?

paragraphs.title: Wisdom of the Heart and the Power of Pleasant Words

easy.explanation: Proverbs 16:21 says, “the sweetness of the lips increaseth learning.”
easy.q: What do the sweetness of the lips increase?

easy.explanation: Proverbs 16:24 says, “Pleasant words are as an honeycomb.”
easy.q: What are pleasant words compared to?

answers: Its end may be the ways of death
easy.explanation: Proverbs 16:25 says that the end of a way that seems right may be “the ways of death.”
easy.q: What may happen to a way that seems right?

answers: It teaches the mouth and adds learning to the lips
medium.explanation: Proverbs 16:23 says, “The heart of the wise teacheth his mouth, and addeth learning to his lips.”
medium.q: How does the wisdom of the heart affect speech?

medium.explanation: The honeycomb is used as a picture of the sweetness of pleasant words.
medium.q: What does “honeycomb” emphasize in the description of pleasant words?

answers: His mouth may create demands or burdens for him
Speech has no connection with labor
medium.explanation: Proverbs 16:26 says, “his mouth craveth it of him,” showing how desire expressed by the mouth can drive a person’s labor.
medium.q: Why may a person’s mouth add to his labor?

answers: Pleasant and healing words versus a misleading way and burdensome speech
challenge.explanation: The passage praises pleasant words but warns about a way that seems right and speech that creates burdens.
challenge.q: What central contrast appears in the passage?

answers: Appearances do not guarantee a good outcome
Every apparently right way leads to life
A person has only one possible way
challenge.explanation: Although the way seems right, its end may be “the ways of death.”
challenge.q: What does “There is a way that seemeth right unto a man” teach about appearances?

answers: They are sweet to the soul and health to the bones
challenge.explanation: Proverbs 16:24 says pleasant words are “sweet to the soul, and health to the bones.”
challenge.q: What connection is made between pleasant words and the body and soul?

easy.explanation: Proverbs 16:27 says, “An ungodly man diggeth up evil.”
easy.q: What does an ungodly man dig up?

easy.explanation: The verse says, “A froward man soweth strife.”
easy.q: What does a froward man sow?

easy.explanation: Proverbs 16:29 says, “A violent man enticeth his neighbour.”
easy.q: Whom does a violent man entice?

medium.explanation: Proverbs 16:28 says, “a whisperer separateth chief friends.”
medium.q: What is the result of a whisperer?
What does “strife” mean in this passage?

answers: Into a way that is not good
medium.explanation: Proverbs 16:29 says he “leadeth him into the way that is not good.”
medium.q: Where does the violent man lead his neighbour?

answers: Evil thoughts and speech lead to enticement, separation, and wrongdoing
challenge.explanation: The verses describe digging up evil, sowing strife, whispering, enticing, and bringing evil to pass.
challenge.q: What sequence describes the development of evil in the passage?

answers: Planning froward things and bringing evil to pass
challenge.explanation: Proverbs 16:30 connects these actions with devising froward things and bringing evil to pass.
challenge.q: What do shutting the eyes and moving the lips suggest?

challenge.explanation: The whisperer separates chief friends, showing the destructive social power of harmful speech.
challenge.q: What is the relationship between harmful speech and human relationships?

answers: When it is found in the way of righteousness
easy.explanation: Proverbs 16:31 says, “The hoary head is a crown of glory, if it be found in the way of righteousness.”
easy.q: When is a hoary head a crown of glory?

easy.explanation: The verse says, “He that is slow to anger is better than the mighty.”
easy.q: What is better than the mighty?

easy.explanation: Proverbs 16:33 concludes, “the whole disposing thereof is of the LORD.”
easy.q: Who determines the outcome of the lot?

medium.explanation: The verse says that he who rules his spirit is better than he who takes a city.
medium.q: What does the verse compare ruling one’s spirit with taking a city?

answers: Patient and not quick to become angry
medium.explanation: Being slow to anger means showing patience and restraint rather than becoming angry quickly.

answers: He casts the lot into the lap
medium.explanation: Proverbs 16:33 says, “The lot is cast into the lap; but the whole disposing thereof is of the LORD.”
medium.q: What does a person do before the LORD determines the outcome?

answers: Old age is honorable when accompanied by righteousness
Old age is honorable only because of years
Old age has no connection with conduct
challenge.explanation: The verse makes the honor of old age dependent on being found in the way of righteousness.
challenge.q: What connection is made between old age and a way of life?

answers: Taking a city versus ruling one’s spirit
challenge.explanation: The verse places conquest of a city below the achievement of ruling one’s own spirit.
challenge.q: What is the central contrast between outward power and inward control?

answers: People cast the lot, but the final determination is of the LORD
challenge.explanation: Although the lot is cast by people, the passage attributes its final outcome to the LORD.
challenge.q: What does the ending teach about human action and final results?
